policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Adopted by Cabinet Decision on December 23, 2025 pursuant to Article 18(1) of the Act on the Promotion of Research, Development, and Utilization of AI-Related Technologies (Act No. 53 of 2025). Implementation and follow-up are led by the AI Strategy Headquarters (chaired by the Prime Minister and comprising all Cabinet ministers) and the AI Strategy Promotion Council, supported by expert consultations through the AI Strategy Expert Panel and benchmark-based monitoring. The plan relies on agile PDCA cycles, voluntary industry initiatives backed by guidelines under Article 13 of the AI Act, risk surveys under Article 16, immediate doubling of AI Safety Institute (AISI) personnel, and alignment with the Science, Technology, and Innovation Basic Plan and the Priority Plan for the Realization of a Digital Society.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: Japan's Basic AI Plan is primarily framed around innovation_enablement, explicitly aiming to make Japan 'the world's easiest country to develop and utilize AI' by balancing innovation promotion with agile, PDCA-based risk management, regulatory reviews, sandboxes, and voluntary trustworthy-AI ecosystems that unlock widespread public and private adoption. Economic_competitiveness is a close runner-up, motivating the overall strategy through industrial revival ('Japan's comeback'), overcoming lagging AI investment, curbing the digital trade deficit, and building domestic growth engines; however, innovation_enablement edges it out because the plan's governance mechanisms themselves are consistently justified as enabling a virtuous cycle of AI utilization and R&D rather than purely zero-sum economic rivalry. National_security (sovereignty, autonomy, defense, and cybersecurity), consumer_public_safety (mitigating fraud, deepfakes, accidents, and public anxiety), labor_transition (analyzing employment impacts and reskilling workers), and fundamental_rights (human-centric dignity, privacy, and non-discrimination) appear as meaningful secondary justifications, with minor social_stability references to disinformation and no existential_catastrophic framing.
